findings.issue_text: `addGuests.handler.ts` uses `&&` instead of `||` for `isTeamAdminOrOwner`, breaking the feature for non-owner team admins.
`email-manager.ts` passes raw `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails`, sending the wrong "scheduled" email to existing attendees if their email is in the input.
`email-manager.ts` and server-side dedup compare emails case-sensitively, failing to match variations like `Bob@X.com` and `bob@x.com`.
`addGuests.schema.ts` server schema does not enforce uniqueness, improperly trusting client-side validation.
`addGuests.handler.ts` uses `console.log` and drops the `err` object in the `catch` block for email errors, making debugging impossible.
`addGuests.handler.ts` omits the `team` field from the constructed `CalendarEvent`, silently preventing team member notifications for team bookings.
Missing translation key `additional_guests` in `common.json` despite being used in components, causing literal keys to render.
`AddGuestsDialog.tsx` error fallback is dead code because `message` is always truthy, and `t(err.message)` fails for non-translation keys.
No tests added for the significant new feature, including auth checks, dedup logic, calendar updates, and edge cases.
`MultiEmail.tsx` has an accessibility issue where multiple inputs share the same `<label htmlFor="emails">` without a corresponding input `id`.
`MultiEmail.tsx` uses `index` as a React key, causing input state to "stick" to the wrong row when items are removed in the middle.
`AddGuestsDialog.tsx` does a silent no-op with no feedback when the email list is empty and the user clicks "Add".
`AddGuestsDialog.tsx` `isInvalidEmail` error banner never clears while the user edits email fields.
`addGuests.handler.ts` stores `name: ""` for new guests, resulting in odd email renderings like "Dear ,".
`addGuests.handler.ts` Prisma include doesn't explicitly select `booking.userPrimaryEmail`, which may fallback to `undefined`.
`AddGuestsDialog.tsx` has a test ID collision where both the submit button and menu item use `add_members`.
`email-manager.ts` sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` to new guests, which is inconsistent with the "Guests Added" feature framing.
`BookingListItem.tsx` uses the misleading menu item id `add_members` instead of `add_guests` for consistency.
`MultiEmailLazy.tsx` comment about component size ("40kb") may be inaccurate and copied from another component.

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `email-manager.ts` passes raw `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails`, sending the wrong "scheduled" email to existing attendees if their email is in the input.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code filters the input `guests` into `uniqueGuests` (excluding already-existing attendees and blacklisted emails) and only creates attendees from `uniqueGuests`. However it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` using the *raw* input list, not `uniqueGuests`. In `email-manager.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails` decides which email to send per attendee using `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` to send `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Therefore, if the caller includes an email that is already an attendee in the input, that existing attendee will match `includes` and incorrectly receive the "scheduled" email. This mismatch is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `email-manager.ts` and server-side dedup compare emails case-sensitively, failing to match variations like `Bob@X.com` and `bob@x.com`.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, deduplication checks `guest === attendee.email` and blacklist checks `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without normalizing case. This allows case-variants of the same email (e.g., `Bob@X.com` vs `bob@x.com`) to be treated as distinct and added. Similarly, in `email-manager.ts` `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` (also case-sensitive), so case-variant matching can misclassify attendees when choosing which email to send. The UI-level uniqueness check in `AddGuestsDialog` also uses a `Set` on raw strings, which is case-sensitive.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `addGuests.handler.ts` uses `console.log` and drops the `err` object in the `catch` block for email errors, making debugging impossible.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the email send is wrapped in a `try/catch` that catches `err` but only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` without logging/including `err` (or rethrowing). This is directly present in the diff and results in losing the actual error details when email sending fails, hindering debugging/observability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `addGuests.handler.ts` omits the `team` field from the constructed `CalendarEvent`, silently preventing team member notifications for team bookings.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the constructed `CalendarEvent` (`evt`) includes organizer, attendees, uid, location, etc., but does not set any `team` information. However, `sendAddGuestsEmails` explicitly checks `calendarEvent.team?.members` and, if present, sends `OrganizerAddGuestsEmail` to each team member. Since `evt` lacks `team`, `calendarEvent.team` will be undefined after `formatCalEvent(calEvent)`, so that loop will never run and team members will not be emailed for team bookings (only the organizer email is sent).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing translation key `additional_guests` in `common.json` despite being used in components, causing literal keys to render.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `t("additional_guests")` being used in `BookingListItem.tsx` and `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, but the locale diff only shows added keys and does not include `additional_guests`. However, since this is a partial diff of `common.json`, it is not verifiable from the diff alone that `additional_guests` is missing from the file overall—it may already exist elsewhere in `common.json` outside the shown hunks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` error fallback is dead code because `message` is always truthy, and `t(err.message)` fails for non-translation keys.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` the `onError` handler builds `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;`. A template-literal always yields a string, so `message` will be truthy even when `err.data?.code` is `undefined` (e.g., producing `"undefined: ..."`). Therefore `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` will never use the fallback, making that fallback effectively dead/unreachable. The claim that `t(err.message)` “fails” for non-translation keys isn’t strictly provable from the diff (it may just return the key), but it can result in poor/untranslated output if `err.message` isn’t a known i18n key.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests added for the significant new feature, including auth checks, dedup logic, calendar updates, and edge cases.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a substantial “add guests” feature (UI, TRPC mutation, email sending, calendar updates), and there are no test files or test changes included. However, the proposed finding is a process/coverage critique rather than a concrete, code-level defect (bug/security/correctness issue) that can be verified as failing behavior from the diff alone. The absence of tests is verifiable, but it is not itself a clear defect introduced by the change under the given criteria.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `MultiEmail.tsx` has an accessibility issue where multiple inputs share the same `<label htmlFor="emails">` without a corresponding input `id`.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the component renders a `<label htmlFor="emails">` but the corresponding `EmailField` instances are not given an `id="emails"` (nor any `id` prop at all). Additionally, the label is rendered once while multiple email inputs are rendered in a list, so even if an `id` existed it would not uniquely associate the label with a specific input. This is a verifiable accessibility defect introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `MultiEmail.tsx` uses `index` as a React key, causing input state to "stick" to the wrong row when items are removed in the middle.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the list renders `value.map((field, index) => (...)` with `<li key={index}>`. Because items can be removed from the middle (`updatedValue.splice(index, 1)`), subsequent items shift indices and therefore keys. React will then reuse component instances for different emails, which can cause per-row component/input state (focus, cursor position, validation/touched state inside `EmailField`, etc.) to attach to the wrong row after deletions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` does a silent no-op with no feedback when the email list is empty and the user clicks "Add".

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, `handleAdd` returns early with `if (multiEmailValue.length === 0) { return; }` and does not set any error state or toast. This state is reachable because `MultiEmail` allows removing email fields via `onClickAddon`, which can splice the last remaining item and set the value to `[]`. If the user removes all fields and clicks “Add”, nothing happens and no feedback is shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` `isInvalidEmail` error banner never clears while the user edits email fields.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `ZAddGuestsInputSchema.safeParse(multiEmailValue)` fails in `handleAdd()`. After that, there is no code path that resets `isInvalidEmail` back to `false` when the user edits the `MultiEmail` fields (the `setValue={setMultiEmailValue}` callback does not touch `isInvalidEmail`). It only resets on the Cancel button click (and the dialog closing). Therefore the error banner will continue to display while the user is correcting inputs, until they cancel/close or successfully submit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `addGuests.handler.ts` stores `name: ""` for new guests, resulting in odd email renderings like "Dear ,".

adjudication.rationale: The diff does set `name: ""` for newly added guests in `addGuests.handler.ts` (via `guestsFullDetails`). However, the proposed finding’s specific impact (“odd email renderings like 'Dear ,'”) is not verifiable from this diff: none of the added/modified email templates shown include any greeting logic, and the referenced `AttendeeScheduledEmail`/`OrganizerScheduledEmail` rendering details are not present here. While an empty name could potentially lead to awkward display names (e.g., in the `to: "${this.attendee.name} <...>"` string), the claimed rendering is speculative based on code not included in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `addGuests.handler.ts` Prisma include doesn't explicitly select `booking.userPrimaryEmail`, which may fallback to `undefined`.

adjudication.rationale: In Prisma, using `findFirst({ where, include: {...} })` returns all scalar fields of `booking` by default; `include` only adds relations and does not require explicitly selecting scalar fields like `userPrimaryEmail`. Additionally, the code already guards with `booking?.userPrimaryEmail ?? organizer.email`, so even if it were missing/undefined it would correctly fall back to `organizer.email` rather than propagating `undefined`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` has a test ID collision where both the submit button and menu item use `add_members`.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the menu action added in `BookingListItem.tsx` uses `id: "add_members"`, while the submit button in `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` uses `data-testid="add_members"`. The diff does not show the menu item being rendered with `data-testid`, nor any mapping from `id` to `data-testid`, so a test ID collision is not directly verifiable from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `email-manager.ts` sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` to new guests, which is inconsistent with the "Guests Added" feature framing.

adjudication.rationale: In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the diff explicitly checks `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` and sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` to those emails, while sending `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` to all other existing attendees. That behavior is consistent with a reasonable interpretation of the feature: newly added guests should receive the normal “you’re scheduled” invite email, and existing attendees should receive a “new guests were added” notification. The proposed finding asserts this is inherently inconsistent with the feature framing, but that’s a product/UX judgment not verifiable as a defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `BookingListItem.tsx` uses the misleading menu item id `add_members` instead of `add_guests` for consistency.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the new menu item is added with `id: "add_members"` while its label and functionality clearly relate to adding guests (`t("additional_guests")`, opens `AddGuestsDialog`). However, nothing in the shown diff indicates that the `id` value is used for correctness, routing, permissions, or any other behavior that would break due to this name. It appears to be a consistency/naming nit (and the same string is also used as a `data-testid`), not a verifiable bug or defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `MultiEmailLazy.tsx` comment about component size ("40kb") may be inaccurate and copied from another component.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only adds a comment in `MultiEmailLazy.tsx` stating the component is “like 40kb”. There’s nothing in the diff that measures or demonstrates the bundle size of `MultiEmail`, so the claim that it “may be inaccurate and copied” is not a verifiable defect. At most, it’s a speculative documentation/style nit, not a bug/correctness/security issue introduced by the change.
